name_en: Miki — a lightly sour, lactic-fermented rice-and-sweet-potato drink from Amami
summary_ja: 米粉とさつまいも、砂糖を発酵させた乳酸菌飲料。祭事で神に捧げる口噛み酒を起源とすると伝わり、できたては甘く、日が経つほど酸味が増していく変化も奄美地域では好まれている。
summary_en: A lactic-fermented drink made from rice flour, sweet potato, and sugar, said to descend from kuchikami-zake once offered to the gods at harvest festivals. It's sweet fresh, but grows more sour by the day — and in Amami, that sourness is often the more prized stage.
source_title: みき 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理

name_en: Buta miso — pork and miso pounded together into a keeping paste, spooned onto rice
summary_ja: ゆでた豚肉を味噌や砂糖と混ぜ合わせてつくる常備菜。奄美地域では落花生やカツオ節も加える。年に一度しめる島豚を余さず食べるため、保存のきく料理として塩漬けなどとともに生まれたと伝わる。
summary_en: Boiled pork is pounded together with miso and sugar into a keeping paste, with peanuts and bonito flakes added in Amami versions. It's said to have grown out of the need to use every part of the one pig a household slaughtered each year, alongside salting and other preserved forms.
source_title: 豚味噌 鹿児島県｜うちの郷土料理
